TREAT YOUR AI AGENTS LIKE NEW EMPLOYEES

I’m obsessed with the idea of agentic-first organizations. 

Businesses that build this early will have a huge advantage. 

Hence my biz name Agentic Org Now. 

Some general advice:

1. AN AGENTIC OPERATING MODEL STARTS WITH WORKFLOWS, NOT AGENTS.

You want to map each workflow step to 4 levels: 

-rules based software

-analytical AI

-generative AI

-agentic AI

Financial reporting needs deterministic rules based systems.

Loans approvals and marketing materials need generative and agentic AI.

2. AI AGENTS NEED TO BE MANAGED LIKE PEOPLE.

Agents are non deterministic, so consistent quality is a real problem.

You have to track, verify and refine them at every step of a workflow.

Just like with new employees.

3. AGENTIC ORGANIZATIONS EVOLVE IN 4 STAGES.

Most businesses are at stage 1.

Employees use GenAI tools for tasks like drafting contracts and summarizing meeting notes.

Stage 4 is when teams of agents run cross functional workflows across the biz.

That’s the goal.

→ Pick one internal workflow this week and label every step as low variance or high variance.

fullText:
Own your personal agent, folks. 

Just built my own little personal agent with @pidotdev's Pi Durable.

I wanted to see how quickly I could build an OpenAI dots clone with open-source tools. 

I am amazed at how quickly I got this off the ground. 

It's proactive. 

It keeps working when you're not watching. It remembers you, runs jobs on a schedule, waits for your approval, and uses its own computer. 

Pi Durable makes that possible.

Every step is checkpointed. I can kill the process mid-task, and My Pi picks up right where it left off.

Memory lives in durable documents. What My Pi learns about me in one Space survives a crash and carries over to every other Space.

Approvals are durable too.

It also has its own computer. Each Space gets a full Linux desktop that My Pi controls with screenshots, mouse, and keyboard. 

The model runs through OpenRouter, so I can swap models without changing anything else. That's all configurable however you like it. 

If you've been wanting your own personal agent, now is a great time to build one. 

I am building this as an experimental ground where I can test new ideas and experiment deeply with proactive personal agents. But I plan to open-source it after testing it a bit and adding more interesting primitives. 

The goal is to make it customizable and easy to build on, so others can experiment with their own personal agent functionalities.
